correctness.rationale: Exact unitary fiber unfolding identifies a(x,s) in {1,2,3}; all three occur on open positive-measure regions. Orthonormal Fourier analysis on Q, with measure 1/4, reduces synthesis to 2×2 Gram matrices having eigenvalues 2±2|cos(πat/4)|. Density gives exact rather than only admissible Riesz bounds. Fiber invertibility yields basis/completeness and exact forbidden classes. A three-interval trigonometric inequality proves unique global minimizers and Taylor expansion proves coefficients. All quantifiers and normalization checked analytically; finite verifier passed, without being treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 revised primary theorem handles only the single offset t=1 and its displayed constants. Its complete six-page proof (especially Theorem 1.1 on p.2 and paired Gram blocks on pp.5–6) does not state the sharp all-real-offset profile, all excluded displacements, unique global optimality, or the four quadratic edge laws. Exact general two-fiber matrix criteria are credited, and the present result gives a motivated complete optimized design phase portrait. Mathematical database searches using exact formula and alternative descriptors did not uncover an equivalent covering claim. Implicit consequences of broad fiber theorems remain a historical priority risk.

value.rationale: The source motivates explicit well-conditioned exponential bases on a fixed nonconvex planar double-tile and supplies only one design. The complete one-parameter phase portrait solves a natural frequency-design question: which offsets fail entirely, which maximize uniform stability, and what exact stability loss occurs close to each resonance. The sharp globally optimal ratio 3+2√2 and three distinct quadratic coefficients are natural practical diagnostics rather than arbitrary numerical slices; proof gives a reusable fiber design method.
